forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 21%. No formal AGI claim from any frontier lab as of 8 Jun. Q1 2026 timelines update (LessWrong/AI Futures) shows researchers compressing capability doubling time from ~5.5 months to ~4 months on the back of Gemini 3, GPT-5.2 and Claude Opus 4.6 — but this raises probability of an AGI-level system existing pre-2030, not the probability of a formal public declaration before 1 Jan 2030. Amodei still anchoring 'within a few years' (≈2027 lean); Hassabis ≈50% by 2030; Altman pointing to 2027-2028. No movement.
forecasts.base_rate: Resolution requires a credible public AGI claim from a major lab OR 3+ leading researchers stating AGI achieved, before 1 Jan 2030 (~3.5 yrs out). Definitional disputes raise the bar; labs historically defer transformational claims until capability is unambiguous.

factors_up.factor: Compressed capability doubling time (~4 months) following Gemini 3 / GPT-5.2 / Claude Opus 4.6
Amodei (Anthropic) maintaining ~2027 AGI timeline; competitive pressure across 6+ frontier-tier labs
AI-automating-AI feedback loops (Anthropic >80% code AI-generated; agentic coding progress)

factors_down.factor: No major lab has issued any formal AGI claim as of 8 June 2026
Definitional ambiguity raises bar for the '3+ senior researchers' clause
Hassabis (DeepMind) still anchoring ~50% by 2030 — not pre-2030

key_uncertainties: Whether internal capability translates to public AGI declarations before 2030
Whether IPO pressure on OpenAI/Anthropic incentivises or deters such claims
Pace of AI-automating-AI loops in 2027-2029
update_triggers: Formal AGI claim from a frontier lab
Public statement by 2+ senior researchers at OpenAI/Anthropic/DeepMind that AGI is achieved
Major step-change on AGI-relevant evals (METR, HLE, ARC-AGI v3)

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Slight nudge down to 23% (from 24%). MCA's latest projection (covered in 2026 consulting industry reporting) still has UK consulting growing 5.7% in 2026 and 7.4% in 2027, with AI as the largest revenue driver for 66% of firms — i.e. AI is augmenting revenue, not contracting it, through 2027. Big Four are shifting to managed-services/outcome-based pricing (PwC targeting 20-25% advisory from managed services; ~25% of McKinsey fees now outcome-based), which compresses billable hours but not necessarily aggregate value. A 33% decline by 2030 from a 2024 baseline still requires a sharp structural break in 2028-2030 that current trajectories do not show.
forecasts.base_rate: Resolution requires consultancy revenue OR employment to fall ≥33% from 2024 baseline by 31 Dec 2030, AI-attributed by 2+ credible analyses. Sector-wide ≥33% declines on 6-year horizons are rare absent a major recession or technology disruption.

factors_up.factor: Outcome-based pricing cannibalising billable hours at top firms (≈25% of McKinsey)
Entry-level analyst hiring already contracting at Big Four
AI tools delivering 25%+ task-speed gains (HBS/BCG study) — pricing pressure on margins

factors_down.factor: UK consulting still forecast +5.7% in 2026 and +7.4% in 2027 (MCA)
AI is largest growth driver for 66% of firms — additive, not substitutive at aggregate level
Managed-services pivot is preserving aggregate revenue even as billable mix shifts

key_uncertainties: Whether AI productivity gains push fee compression below the revenue floor by 2028-2030
Whether 'economic consultancy' is interpreted narrowly (econ policy/macro shops) or broadly (Big Four advisory)
Recession risk through 2027-2029
update_triggers: First Big Four annual revenue decline tied explicitly to AI
Layoffs of >10% at MBB or Big Four advisory
Two credible analyses attributing ≥15% sector decline to AI

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Nudge up marginally to 5% (from 4%). PollCheck 7-poll moving average (6 Jun): Reform 26.6%, Conservatives 18.6%, Labour 18.4%, Greens 15.1%, Lib Dems 12.3%. Labour now in third on the moving average, still well behind Reform. With ~3-3.5 years to the latest possible GE (Dec 2029), recovery is mathematically possible but the gap to Reform is wide and the trajectory remains downward. The very slight uplift reflects (i) long horizon allowing reversion, (ii) FPTP can still deliver 'largest party' status to Labour at lower vote shares if Reform/Conservative vote splits in key marginals, (iii) historical incumbency-recovery patterns.
forecasts.base_rate: UK governing party with mid-term polling in low-20s recovering to 'largest party' is uncommon but not unprecedented (1992, 2005 partial parallels). With 3+ years to go, fundamentals can shift.

factors_up.factor: 3-3.5 years to GE — meaningful time for reversion
FPTP can deliver largest party at ~25% vote share if right-wing vote splits 3 ways
Incumbency advantages (fiscal events, agenda-setting)

factors_down.factor: Labour at 18.4% on PollCheck 7-poll average — third place
Reform at 26.6% and consolidating right-wing vote
Approval ratings approaching previous-government nadir

key_uncertainties: Whether Reform vote consolidates or fragments by 2028-2029
Conservative recovery dynamics and any leadership change
Economic conditions through 2027-2029 (CPI, growth, employment)
update_triggers: Labour returning above 25% in 7-poll average
Reform falling below 22% sustained
Major Labour leadership change or coalition signal

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 78%. With ~8.5 years of runway and capability doubling time now compressed to ~4 months on the latest models, the probability of at least one frontier lab declaring AGI before 2035 remains very high. Even on Hassabis's ~50% by 2030 prior, conditional probability of 2030-2034 declaration is high. Main downside risks remain definitional gatekeeping, compute/energy bottlenecks, or major policy shock (regulatory pause).
forecasts.base_rate: 8.5-year window with multiple frontier labs racing; conditional on current capability trajectory, base rate for a public AGI declaration in this window is high.

factors_up.factor: Compressed capability doubling time (~4 months)
Multiple labs racing — at least one likely to declare in this window
AI-automating-AI feedback effects compound over 8+ years

factors_down.factor: Definitional disputes could delay public declarations
Compute, energy and chip bottlenecks
Regulatory pause/safety incident risk

key_uncertainties: Whether progress saturates around current paradigm or compounds via agentic/RL self-improvement
Geopolitical disruptions (Taiwan, sanctions on AI hardware)
Definitional consensus on 'AGI achieved'
update_triggers: Formal AGI claim from any frontier lab
Sustained slowdown in eval gains across multiple benchmarks
Major regulatory action restricting frontier training

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 8%. AEI China-Taiwan update (5 Jun) reports continued PLA modernisation: 2026 defence budget +7% to ~$278B, two new Type 055 destroyers commissioned, Strait Thunder 2025A and Justice Mission 2025 exercises rehearsing port blockades and LNG-facility strikes. Taiwan responding with LNG-reserve build-up to 14 days and convoy exercises. Activity remains in the 'pressure short of conflict' band, not initiation. ~3.5 years of remaining horizon. No movement.
forecasts.base_rate: Major-power-initiated blockade/invasion against a US-aligned partner is a low-frequency event; PLA window-of-opportunity arguments cite mid-2027 onward, but most analysts price <10% over 5 years.

factors_up.factor: Continued PLA buildup (+7% budget, Type 055s, amphibious capacity)
Blockade-specific exercises rehearsing LNG / port targeting
US political-cycle uncertainty creating windows of opportunity

factors_down.factor: Economic costs to PRC of blockade/invasion remain prohibitive
Taiwan hardening (LNG reserves, convoy drills, US arms sales)
No mobilisation indicators consistent with imminent initiation

key_uncertainties: Xi succession/health and CCP politics through 2027-2029
US deterrent posture under shifting administrations
Whether blockade is treated as lower-cost coercion option
update_triggers: PLA full-scale mobilisation or visible logistics buildup
Major Taiwan Strait incident with kinetic exchange
US-China decoupling escalation (chip embargo + reciprocal action)

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Nudge up slightly to 6% (from 5%). April 2026 CPI at 2.8% (down from 3.3% in March), reflecting fading energy-shock effects from the earlier Iran conflict. Next ONS release (17 Jun) covers May 2026. Trajectory is downward but the gap from 2.8% to <2.0% is still ~0.8pp and only ~7 monthly readings remain (May-Nov 2026, reported by Dec 2026 / early Jan 2027). Below-2% prints require a sharper disinflation than Bank of England or market consensus expects.
forecasts.base_rate: UK CPI undershooting 2% over a sustained period has happened in disinflationary cycles (2014-16, 2020), but in the current cycle CPI has remained above 2% throughout 2025-26. Probability of a single sub-2% print remains low absent a demand shock.

factors_up.factor: Headline CPI falling 0.5pp month-on-month (March 3.3 → April 2.8)
Energy base effects unwinding through summer 2026
Weak UK demand / fading wage growth pressure

factors_down.factor: Services inflation remains sticky around 4%
BoE central forecast keeps CPI above 2% through 2026
Only ~7 monthly prints remain before resolution window closes

key_uncertainties: Energy market volatility through summer 2026
Services inflation persistence
Sterling and import-price pass-through
update_triggers: May 2026 CPI print (17 Jun) materially below 2.5%
BoE downgrading near-term CPI path below 2%
Sharp commodity / sterling appreciation

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Nudge down to 68% (from 72%). Latest tracking (Variety 2026 box-office outlook; Polymarket implied 54.5% for highest-grossing 2026 domestic film) has BND 'comfortably crossing $1B worldwide' but commentary stops short of asserting $1.5B is base case. Releases 31 Jul 2026, leaving 5 months of theatrical window in-year. $1.5B would put it above No Way Home's $1.92B inflation-adjusted but ahead of most solo MCU films. Probability remains favourable given character strength and release slot, but the $1.5B bar is genuinely demanding.
forecasts.base_rate: Spider-Man: No Way Home grossed $1.92B; Far From Home $1.13B. A $1.5B opening-year is in the top quartile of MCU outcomes; conditional on a Tom Holland MCU Spider-Man relaunch with No Way Home goodwill, probability is materially above base rate.

factors_up.factor: Polymarket implying 54.5% chance of #1 2026 domestic film
Tom Holland MCU Spider-Man franchise post-No Way Home halo
Late-July opening — full summer + holiday-quarter runway in 2026

factors_down.factor: Variety / industry framing only confirms $1B baseline, not $1.5B
Competition from Avengers: Doomsday and other tentpoles
China market access uncertainty for Marvel titles

key_uncertainties: Opening weekend performance
Critical reception and word-of-mouth multiplier
China release decision and revenue share
update_triggers: Pre-sales / first weekend grosses
Doomsday opening as a leading indicator for the MCU slate
China release confirmation

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 99%. As of May 2026 reporting (The AI Corner, SaaStr, Sacra, Epoch AI), Anthropic ARR is ~$45B and OpenAI ~$33B — combined ~$78B already running above the $70B threshold by mid-year. Note OpenAI dispute that Anthropic's reseller-gross accounting overstates by ~$8B; even at the haircut, combined sits at ~$70B today with 6+ months of growth ahead. Resolution requires Q4 2026 ARR sum to exceed $70B — by current run-rate and growth trajectory, this is near-certain absent a major business shock.
forecasts.base_rate: Both companies grew >2x year-on-year through 2025-26; conditional on no enterprise demand collapse, Q4 ARR materially above mid-year is base case.

factors_up.factor: Combined ARR already ~$78B in May 2026 reporting
Both companies growing >50% YoY
Enterprise contract expansions continue (Anthropic API-driven)

factors_down.factor: OpenAI accounting dispute could reduce Anthropic headline figure by ~$8B
Macroeconomic enterprise spending pullback risk
Definitional disputes over what counts as 'credible' Q4 2026 ARR

key_uncertainties: Exact ARR-counting methodology used at resolution
Q4 enterprise contract renewal cycles
Any major safety incident or regulatory action
update_triggers: Quarterly disclosures from OpenAI / Anthropic
Bloomberg / The Information ARR updates
Any sharp slowdown in token growth or enterprise wins

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 35%. OBR March 2026 EFO has real GDP per person at ~1.1% per year to 2030, with productivity growth assumed to recover to 1% in the medium term and labour supply growth dropping to 0.5% by 2030 — implying headline real GDP growth in the 1.5-1.6% range at the end of the forecast horizon. IFS projects 1.4% average from 2026 onwards. A decade average above 1.5% therefore requires sustained productivity rebound through the 2030s — plausible on an AI-productivity upside scenario, but central path is at or just below 1.5%. No new data this weekend; hold central.
forecasts.base_rate: UK trend GDP growth has been ≈1.3-1.6% post-2010; 1990s and 2000s averaged ≈2.5-3%. Decade-mean above 1.5% is plausible but at upper edge of recent experience.

factors_up.factor: Productivity tailwind from AI adoption in 2030s
OBR medium-term productivity recovery assumption (1.0%)
Public investment programmes coming online late-2020s

factors_down.factor: Labour supply growth falling to 0.5% — demographic drag
OBR per-capita growth only 1.1% to 2030
Fiscal-consolidation drag through 2027-2030

key_uncertainties: Whether AI-productivity translates to UK measured GDP growth
Immigration policy / labour-supply trajectory post-2030
Capex response from energy transition and AI infrastructure
update_triggers: OBR autumn 2026 EFO productivity revision
Decisive evidence on AI-productivity in UK firm data
Material immigration policy shifts
